title: World boss: a low first reading isn't damage
what: While a boss's bar slides in it can read nearly empty. If nobody has hit it yet and the bar then reads much fuller twice in a row, the low reading is dropped.
gain: The fight's clock starts at the real first hit. In 5 of 59 world fights in real logs the low reading stuck; one started 15.5 s late and read as 2 s and 178,203 DPS.
risk: A boss that really is low and reads much fuller, in the bar's own red, before anyone hits it would count from the fuller reading until a low one is confirmed.
tested: Bench tested on readings from real logs, not tried in a game

title: Don't copy the whole screen on the graphics card
what: aLogs keeps the newest picture of the screen on the graphics card and copies out only the spots its readers ask for. Until now it first copied the whole screen into a picture of its own, each time the screen changed and a reader was due: up to about 60 times a second with Sanctum Helper's map tracking. With this on it copies the spots straight out of the screen's own picture and hands that back to Windows as soon as they are started. Only where aLogs captures the screen rather than the game window (every Windows 10 PC).
gain: Unknown until tested in a game. One whole-screen copy less on the graphics card per picture taken (33 MB at 4K, about 2 GB a second at 60 a second). It should matter most when the game already uses the whole card.
risk: If the screen stops changing just as a reader asks for a new spot, that reader waits for the next picture; after 0.3 s the capture starts again, which takes a moment. A spot copied while the card is very busy could show a slightly newer picture than its time says.
tested: Measured outside the game on one Windows 10 PC at 4K (10 Nov): as many pictures as with it off (282 and 281 in 300 rounds), as many spots read (98 and 98), none black, and aLogs' own time per picture down from 0.14 to 0.06 ms. Not tried in a game yet: the frame rate is the open question.

title: Let the game go first on the graphics card
what: aLogs asks Windows to do its copies on the graphics card after the game's own work, at the lowest priority a program may give itself. Off puts it back to normal at once.
gain: Unknown until tested in a game. When the card is fully used, aLogs' copies should no longer be done ahead of the game's frames.
risk: When the card is very busy, pictures reach the DPS meter and Sanctum Helper later than now, so bars, the map and result screens could be read late. On result screens the card already took up to 0.85 s to hand over a whole picture.

title: Check the game's icon row less often while nothing changes
what: The button over the game looks at the game's icon row 8 times a second to know when to show and hide. With this on, once the row has been there for 2 seconds it looks 4 times a second, and goes straight back to 8 when the row goes missing, the mouse pointer appears or disappears, the game window moves or changes size, you come back to the game, or you press the button.
gain: Half as many small copies of the picture off the graphics card while you play with the icon row showing. How much that helps the game is unknown until tested in a game.
risk: The button can hide up to a quarter of a second later than now when the icon row goes away (about 0.75 to 1.25 seconds instead of 0.75 to 1.0). It never hides sooner and it shows again exactly as fast as now. Its slide between the keyboard and controller positions can also start up to a quarter of a second later.
tested: Bench tested the timing rules, not tried in a game

title: Priority High no longer puts aLogs ahead of the game
what: General Settings › Priority set to High runs aLogs, the DPS meter and Sanctum Helper above the game when Windows has to choose. With this on, High gives them the same priority as the game, never more. Low and Normal are unchanged, so this does nothing unless your Priority is High. It takes effect within 3 seconds of turning it on or off, no restart needed.
gain: When the processor is full, the game is no longer made to wait for aLogs. Unknown until tested in a game.
risk: On a PC whose processor is full during fights, the DPS meter may get less time than with High today, which could mean slower or missed reads. Unknown until tested in a game.
tested: Bench tested which priority each setting gives, not tried in a game

title: Text readers give way to the game
what: The meter reads text on screen (names, numbers, result screens) with small helper programs that use Windows' own text reading. With this on they run at Windows' Below Normal priority, so when the processor is full the game goes first. Helpers already running follow the switch within a minute, both when it is turned on and off.
gain: Unknown until tested in a game. It can only matter when every processor core is busy; then the game should stutter less while text is read.
risk: On a PC with a full processor the text reads take longer, so names, a result screen or the boss's HP number could be read later than now. With a core free nothing changes.
tested: Bench tested with a stand-in helper: it starts at Below Normal with the switch on, at Normal with it off, and a running one moves both ways. Not tried in a game.

title: Save diagnostic pictures off the reading loop
what: The meter keeps pictures for finding bugs later: a sample of a screen now and then, the boss bar when a fight starts, end screens. Saving a whole 4K picture takes a few tenths of a second, and until now the reading loop waited for it. With this on they are saved by a worker of their own; two can wait in line, and with the line full the picture is saved the old way, so none is dropped. The pictures kept as proof of a run, and the ones written together with a note about a lost bar, are saved as before.
gain: Unknown until tested in a game. Each such picture stops holding up the looks by a few tenths of a second (at 30 looks a second that was up to ten or so missed looks per picture).
risk: A diagnostic picture reaches the disk a few tenths of a second later than now. If the meter is ended by force rather than closed, the one or two pictures still waiting are lost. While a picture is being packed the looks can still run a little slower, as both share one processor core's worth of the meter.
tested: Bench tested with made-up pictures: the saved files are identical with it on and off, also when the picture is drawn over right after; a full line saves in the old way; a failed save is one line in the log and the next picture still saves. Not tried in a game.

title: After an Egg Heist match: whole screen only when it is read
what: For 45 seconds after an Egg Heist match is sent the meter takes the whole screen on every look, because the rank screen can come at any moment. With this on it takes the whole screen only on the looks a screen read is made from (each read there still gets the whole screen, so the rank screen is kept just the same), and for 20 seconds after an Interlink fight ends. The looks in between take the top part only.
gain: Unknown until tested in a game. Most looks in those 45 seconds handle the top 42% of the screen and not all of it: about 19 MB less per look at 4K inside the meter. The copying on the graphics card only drops as well when "Whole screen kept for 0.3 s" is also on.
risk: A screen read in those 45 seconds can start one look later than now: 0.05 s, or 0.25 s when the meter is at its slow pace (where reads are a second apart anyway). The rank screen would be read that much later.
tested: Bench tested against made-up states: with it off every look asks for the whole screen as today; with it on only the looks with a read do; outside the 45 seconds nothing differs. Not tried in a game.

title: Whole screen kept for 0.3 s, not 2 s
what: When a reader asks for the whole screen, aLogs keeps copying the whole screen for 2 seconds after its last use, in case it is wanted again. With a read every second or so that means whole-screen copies all the time. With this on it stops after 0.3 seconds, and goes back to copying only the spots being read.
gain: Unknown until tested in a game. Between screen reads that are more than 0.3 s apart the graphics card copies only the read spots (the top part or less) and not the whole screen: at 4K 33 MB less per picture.
risk: Each read that needs the whole screen again waits for its own copy: usually 10 to 35 ms, up to 0.12 s on a busy graphics card, after which that look is skipped and the next one reads. Reads closer together than 0.3 s are not affected.
tested: Bench tested with a stand-in for the shared picture: the whole screen stays asked for 2 s with it off and 0.3 s with it on, and reads 0.25 s apart keep it. Not tried in a game.

title: Calmer pace in Egg Heist runs and Interlink rooms
what: In an Egg Heist run or an Interlink room with no boss bar up, the meter looks 20 times a second and reads the screen's text up to 10 times a second while the picture keeps changing. With this on, while nothing there can't wait, it reads text at most twice a second, and outside Interlink rooms looks 10 times a second (Interlink rooms keep 20, as their boss bars start timed fights). Today's pace comes straight back when the top of the screen jumps or fades to black, when a screen is up, while inputs are held, while a result is read or sent, during automatic clicks, while names are read, for 45 seconds after a fight and for 90 seconds after an Egg Heist match.
gain: Unknown until tested in a game. Up to 8 fewer text reads a second, and in Egg Heist half the looks. Each text read is a few to some tens of milliseconds of processor time.
risk: A screen that appears without a fade and without a clear jump of the top of the screen is read up to 0.4 s later than now. Outside Interlink a boss bar is seen up to 0.05 s later. An Egg Heist end screen normally follows a fade, which puts today's pace back for 10 seconds; if that fade were missed, the hold on your inputs would start up to about 0.45 s later.
tested: Bench tested against made-up states: off is today's pace everywhere; on, 22 states that can't wait keep today's pace, and a jump or a black screen puts it back for 1.5 and 10 seconds. Not tried in a game.

title: Tabbed out: search for a boss bar twice a second
what: With no fight on, the meter searches the whole picture for a boss bar on every look. When there is red or orange on screen that isn't a bar, each search takes 85 to 110 ms. With this on, while the game is not the window in front and no fight is on, that search runs at most twice a second. The places a bar has been before are still checked on every look.
gain: Unknown until tested in a game. Worked out from a measurement outside the game at 4K: a tenth to a fifth of a processor core while tabbed out with red or orange on screen; nothing otherwise. It does not touch the larger tabbed-out cost found in one log, the Party screen being re-read every few seconds, which is left as it is so a team is never sent out of date.
risk: A boss bar that shows up in a new place while you are tabbed out is found up to 0.5 s later, so a fight that starts while you are tabbed out could start that much late.
tested: Bench tested against made-up states: off, every look searches; on, every other look at four looks a second, and every look again with the game in front, a fight on or a bar known. Not tried in a game.

title: Diagnostic pictures: the saving worker at lowest priority
what: Only does something together with "Save diagnostic pictures off the reading loop". The worker that saves those pictures then runs at Windows' lowest priority, so the game and everything else go first.
gain: Unknown until tested in a game. On a full processor the game gets the time the saving would have taken.
risk: The worker and the reading loop take turns inside the meter. If Windows keeps the worker waiting while it holds the turn, the reading loop waits with it: looks could stall for longer than they do today, which is the opposite of the aim. That is why it is its own switch.
tested: Bench tested that the worker's priority changes and changes back, and that the reading loop's does not. The stall has not been measured. Not tried in a game.

title: Say why the boss kill sound wasn't used
what: After each world boss is caught, the log says whether aLogs was listening, when it last heard the game, and how close the best match to the kill sound came. Nothing about the fight changes.
gain: The sound wasn't used once in 24 log files, so fights fall back on 3 s before the Catch Countdown. This shows why, so it can be fixed.
risk: None found; one more log line per boss caught.
tested: Bench tested with made-up values, not tried in a game

title: Egg Heist: don't copy the whole screen
what: During an Egg Heist run the DPS meter copied the whole screen on every look, 20 times a second, for something it no longer does. With this on it copies only the top of the screen and the spots it reads there. The end and rank screens still get the whole screen when they show.
gain: About 620 MB a second less copied at 4K during a run (of about 800 in all). One player's game lost FPS in runs; this is the biggest part of what aLogs copies there.
risk: If an end or rank screen is first seen later than before, its numbers are read a moment later; inputs are still held until they're read.
tested: Checked against the code and a test, not tried in a game

title: Don't redraw overlay text that hasn't changed
what: During a fight the DPS meter redraws its text over the game 4 times a second, also the labels that still say the same: the text, its outline and its soft shadow are made again and the same picture is handed to Windows again. With this on, a label with the same text, size and colour reuses its finished picture, and a window that already shows that exact picture at that exact spot is left alone. Every window is still shown afresh at least every 2 seconds, and at once after you tab back in, drag it or it was hidden.
gain: In a made-up 80 seconds with a fight: 94 label pictures made instead of 298 and 143 window updates instead of 385, with every pixel, spot and moment on screen the same. How much CPU that is in a real fight is unknown until tested in a game; once a minute the log says how many were made and reused, and the milliseconds spent.
risk: If something other than the meter hides or moves one of its windows during a fight, it can take up to 2 seconds to come back instead of a quarter of a second. Nothing else is known to differ.
tested: Bench tested with a made-up fight (the same pixels at the same spots on all 5,334 looks), not tried in a game

title: The overlay rests while nothing is showing
what: The DPS meter looks after its windows over the game every 15 ms, also when none of them is showing. With this on, it looks every 50 ms while there is no fight and nothing is showing, moving, fading or waiting to show. As soon as a fight, a notice, the example or the attack warning begins, it's back to every 15 ms.
gain: About 20 looks a second instead of 66 outside fights: 933 fewer of 5,334 in a made-up 80 seconds. Nothing changes during a fight. How much CPU that saves is unknown until tested in a game; once a minute the log counts both kinds of look.
risk: Something that begins while nothing is showing can appear up to 50 ms after it began instead of up to 15 (30 ms later was the most in the bench test). A fight's numbers still change 4 times a second, but that rhythm can start a few ms earlier or later, so now and then one number shows a quarter of a second apart from where it would have, as already happens from one fight to the next.
tested: Bench tested with a made-up fight, tab-outs, a drag and notices (the same pictures in the same order), not tried in a game

title: Egg Heist: reject impossible rank gains
what: A gain read on the rank screen above that rank's limit in the game's data (90, 180, 270, then 360) counts as a misread and isn't sent to your profile. The total still is.
gain: A misread number can't show on your profile as your last gain. None has been seen yet: all 14 gains in real logs were within the limit.
risk: That this limit caps one match's gain is inferred from its name and size, not confirmed. If it means something else, a real bigger gain wouldn't show as your last gain.
tested: Checked against real logs (14 gains kept), not tried in a game

title: No retry of a waiting record during a boss fight
what: A record that couldn't be sent (no connection, or the site was busy) is tried again every minute, and every try opens and shrinks its screenshots again. With this on, a retry that comes due while the DPS meter is following a boss fight waits until the fight is over, 5 minutes at most. A new record is still sent the moment it's ready, in a fight too, and takes the waiting ones along. Nothing waits right after the meter starts.
gain: No opening and shrinking of screenshots and no failing connection in the middle of a fight because of older records. In a made-up 15 minutes, the first 7 without a connection: 4 tries instead of 9, and the same records delivered. It only matters while a record is waiting; unknown until tested in a game.
risk: A waiting record can reach the leaderboard later: up to 5 minutes per wait, and with fight after fight it is tried every 6 minutes instead of every minute. In the bench test both records arrived 2 minutes later than with this off. Records stay saved the whole time and are sent after a restart as before. Only fights the DPS meter follows count.
tested: Bench tested with made-up records, fights and a made-up connection (nothing lost, the same bytes delivered), not tried in a game
